fields.Location: Westbrook High School (Room 114), 125 Stroudwater St. (Hybrid via Zoom)

note: This summary highlights the meeting's key discussions and decisions, with direct quotes and timestamps for verification — it is not a substitute for watching the full meeting. Six of seven regular members were present (Katy Rice absent); no student representatives attended (one graduated, one on summer vacation). A brief special meeting for administrator appointments; every vote passed unanimously. Summarization necessarily condenses and selects; for complete context, nuance, and anything not covered, watch the full video at the link above. (Produced by: WestbrookCurrents.com)
attendance: Present: Chair Andrea Mancuso, Allison Brunette, Erin Cavallaro, Noreen Poitras, Brooke Reed, Dr. Flynn Ross. Absent: Vice Chair Katy Rice.

blocks.x: Westbrook High School has moved from a leadership structure with three co-principals, in place for seven years, to one principal and two assistant principals. Jeff Garrett, previously a co-principal, moves into the principal role. Patrick Colgan, also previously a co-principal, becomes an assistant principal. Both are internal transfers under the administrators' collective bargaining agreement (a union contract). The second assistant principal role is filled by nomination later in this meeting (see 9.1.3 below).
The state's new bell-to-bell cell phone ban takes effect for the new school year. A community technology forum is planned for August 18 at Westbrook High School.

Greater Portland Metro will provide free bus passes to Westbrook High School students. This follows advocacy from Mayor David Morse and the Westbrook Education Foundation. It is pending the City Council's second reading, the final and binding vote, the following week. The passes are meant to help students within the school's roughly 1.5-mile walking radius get to school. They are also meant to give students broader access to part-time jobs and Greater Portland destinations.
Chair's Remarks — Context on the Metro Bus Pass Initiative

Chair Mancuso gave an extended reflection on how the bus-pass initiative came together. She credited two ad hoc (temporary) transportation subcommittees. She also credited persistent advocacy from Principal Garrett and the high school team. She credited the district's chronically understaffed Transportation Department too. The department was fully staffed only once in the past six years, for less than a full year. She credited the Westbrook Education Foundation and City Hall for recognizing the project's broader community transit value, not just its school-transportation benefit.
9.1.1 — Nomination of Bethany Connolly as Assistant Superintendent, First and Final Approval

Moved by Erin Cavallaro, seconded by Noreen Poitras. Cavallaro served on the hiring committee along with Dr. Flynn Ross. Cavallaro praised the strength of the candidate pool and Connolly's experience as principal of Skillin Elementary School in South Portland (nine years). Cavallaro noted demographic similarities to Sacarappa School. Dr. Lancia added that Connolly previously taught at, and served as assistant principal of, Lincoln Middle School. Connolly was not present (on an anniversary trip) and will be introduced in person at the August 12 meeting.
Approved 6–0. Moved by Erin Cavallaro, seconded by Noreen Poitras.
9.1.2 — Nomination of Tyler Pelletier as Assistant Principal, Westbrook Middle School, First and Final Approval

This replaces Sam Chadow, who resigned. Moved by Erin Cavallaro, seconded by Noreen Poitras. Pelletier, present at the meeting, introduced himself (seven years at South Portland Middle School and Dyer Elementary School).
Approved 6–0. Moved by Erin Cavallaro, seconded by Noreen Poitras.
9.1.3 — Nomination of Carrie Fardella as Assistant Principal, Westbrook High School, First and Final Approval

This was added to the agenda at the start of the meeting (moved by Erin Cavallaro, seconded by Dr. Flynn Ross, 6–0). Moved by Erin Cavallaro, seconded by Noreen Poitras. Poitras, who served on the interview committee, praised Fardella's enthusiasm. Fardella was present and introduced by the Chair. She said she was born and raised in Westbrook and has taught in the district for 34 years. She spoke about the day-to-day reality of students arriving at school with frozen feet from the 1.5-mile walk. This ties directly back to the Metro bus pass initiative discussed above.
Approved 6–0. Moved by Erin Cavallaro, seconded by Noreen Poitras.

“People at the high school, teachers, administrators, secretaries, custodians, we have change socks for kids whose feet are frozen from walking a mile and a half. We have a coat closet where there are boots that are dry and new socks that we can put on … this is a game changer for our school as far as attendance … this will level the playing field.”

August 12, 5:00 PM: Finance Committee resumes its monthly schedule (Room 114). August 12, 6:00 PM (earlier than usual, for this month only): regular School Committee meeting, right after the Finance Committee, also in Room 114. August 27–28: staff back-to-school days. August 31: first day of school for all students except kindergartners and preschoolers. The Chair also flagged the City Council's second and final reading on the Metro bus pass program. It is set for Monday, August 3 at 6:00 PM. The Chair encouraged school-community members to attend in support.

Dr. Lancia asked families to watch email, the district website, and social media for back-to-school information, including open house dates. Dr. Lancia also encouraged anyone in the community to contact registrar Mrs. Lentz at Westbrook High School over the summer if a child needs to register for school.
9.2 — Adjourn Into Executive Session — Contract Negotiations
The committee adjourned directly from executive session with no further public action. An executive session is a closed, private session allowed by state law for certain topics.
Approved 6–0, moved by Erin Cavallaro, seconded by Noreen Poitras.
